glosses: A tangled mess; an entanglement, a snarl, a tangle.

examples.text: Mr. Urquhart was in sic a ravel after it that when he gies out the first line o' the hunder and nineteenth psalm for singing, says he, 'And so on to the end.'

glosses: A confusing, intricate, or perplexing situation; a complication.

To entwine or tangle (something) confusedly; to entangle.

examples.text: For the faith of very many men seems a duty so weak and indifferent, is so often untwisted by violence, or ravelled and entangled in weak discourses, or so false and fallacious by its mixture of interest, that though men usually put most confidences in the pretences of faith, yet no pretences are most unreasonable.

glosses: Often followed by up: to form (something) out of discrete elements, like weaving fabric from threads; to knit.

examples.text: [Magazine staffer about his political team:] Pencils at the ready, keen brains agleam behind intelligent horn rims, these experts spread out to ravel the loose ends of White-Housing, web-spinning spiders for [the presidential candidate].

glosses: To unwind (a reel of thread, a skein of yarn, etc.); to pull apart (cloth, a seam, etc.); to fray, to unpick, to unravel; also, to pull out (a string of yarn, a thread, etc.) from a piece of fabric, or a skein or reel.

examples.text: [Y]ou ſhall haue one vvoman knit more in a hovver then any man can Rauell agen in ſeauen and tvventy yeare.

glosses: To confuse or perplex (someone or something).

examples.text: Make you to rouell^([sic]) all this matter out / That I eſſentially am not in madneſſe, / But mad in craft, […]

glosses: To destroy or ruin (something), like unravelling fabric.

examples.text: [S]helter, ſhelter, if you be ſeene / All's ravell'd out agen: ſtand there private, / And you'le find the very opportunity / To call you forth, and place you at the Table.

examples.text: [G]ive him a broad ſide my brave boyes with your Pikes, branch me his ſkin in Flovvers like a Sattin, and betvveene ever Flovver a mortall cut, your Royalty ſhall ravell, […]

examples.text: But the real work of the First Thursday Foundation is remembering, and its biggest gift is knitting back together lives raveled by loss.
